items.description: R1: track_build.py follows a green build into the Argo CD deploy it triggers — "wait until the deploy the green build triggers has rolled" — generic for every Argo-deployed repo, not KubeCoder-only. After a green build that printed a pin line (JenkinsPipelineUtils vars/cicd.groovy:133, the pin line of every writeVersionPins caller), the tracker returns only once every Application touched by that handoff has rolled the pinned commit or a descendant, and its summary reports each app. The pin line's owner, masked as `****` in the console (KubeCoder/Build-Main #551), does not stop the follow.

R2: "By default." The follow into Argo CD happens with no flag given. A command line that works today (e.g. `track_build.py KubeCoder/Build-Main --hash <sha>`, KubeCoder docs/operations/deploy-operations.md:84) now waits for the roll.

items.area: R3 — git only from the environment's clone
items.description: R3: git questions are answered only from the deploy repo's clone in /work. If the clone isn't there, the tracker stops with a message that the repo isn't there and should be added. Per ruling D1, the stop comes with a distinct exit status (the build was green, the deploy is untracked). The message names every missing deploy repo, each with the exact `git clone` line to run now, and says to declare the repo in the environment's `.kubecoder/config.yaml` for next time.

R4: prd promotions are tracked too. Every green Promote-PRD run, the record-only re-run included, prints a handoff line naming pvginkel/KubeCoderDeploy, the commit and the `prd` branch, in a form that shows whether the run moved `prd`. Today the job prints none: KubeCoderDeploy Jenkinsfile.promote:98, :100, :129. Pointed at a promotion that moved `prd`, the tracker follows the Applications that track `prd` (kubecoder-prd) to the promoted commit.

R5: when none of the tracked green builds prints a handoff line, the tracker says so, in words that tell the agent it may have to fix a pipeline for the tracker to follow the Argo CD deployment. It then exits with the build's own result, not a failure.
R6: the default `--appear-timeout` is 5 minutes, up from 30 s (DockerImages kube-coder-dev-local-home/track_build.py:366-371), and the help text agrees.

Only the Applications that roll the handoff are waited on: those whose source repoURL and targetRevision match the pushed repo and branch, and, for a pin line, whose helm valueFiles name a pinned file, in either the `../config/<stage>/values.yaml` form or the `$values/config/<stage>/values.yaml` form. A KubeCoder/Build-Main pin commit waits on kubecoder-dev and not on kubecoder-prd, which tracks `prd`. A dev-only pin to a repo whose dev and prd apps share `main` (keycloak's shape) waits on the dev app only. A three-source upstream-chart app is matched through its `ref: values` source.

For a handoff that pushed a new commit, the tracker does not declare an app rolled on the strength of Argo's compared revision alone. An app that is OutOfSync at the new commit, with its previous operation finished, is still waited on. An app that Argo reports Synced at the commit or a descendant, with no operation running and health not Progressing, is done even when the commit rendered no change and so no new operation ran.

The tracker stops, with a message saying what happened, rather than waiting indefinitely when: Argo CD does not pick up the commit within a deadline (push-only sync, a lost webhook); the roll is not done by the roll deadline; an app carries a SyncError condition; an app has no automated sync policy (today argocd-prd); or a handoff matches no Application. The script's exit-status documentation covers every outcome it can end with.

When a followed app's sync fails, ends unhealthy, stops on a SyncError, or is not done at the roll deadline, the tracker saves into `--log-dir`, beside failing builds' console logs, the operation message, the conditions, the failed or unhealthy resources, and the app's `tf-presync-<app>` hook Job log from argocd-hooks. The summary names the saved file.

The tracker reads Argo CD state from the Kubernetes API with the environment's default `~/.kube/config`. It runs under the dev container's system python3, without kubectl or the iac sidecar, and writes nothing to Argo CD or the cluster.

Ansible's copy of the script and its test (tools/ai_workflow/) are deleted, and DockerImages kube-coder-dev-local-home/ is the only source. The Ansible paragraphs describing the copy (docs/live-infra-access.md:57-59, docs/design-philosophy.md:62-63) point at DockerImages. No coverage is lost: every case of the deleted Ansible test has its successor in the DockerImages suite.

DockerImages' `kc project test` runs the tracker's suite (today it declares only backup-server and architecture: DockerImages .kubecoder/project.yaml:20-22), and the suite is green. It includes the tests for the Argo CD follow, the handoff parsing, the missing-clone stop, the roll deadline, the report on a handoff that pushed nothing and the default appear timeout.

KubeCoder's docs no longer have agents confirm the roll by hand. docs/operations/deploy-operations.md section "A green build is not a rolled dev" (:92-99) says the tracker waits for the roll and what its stop exits mean. Three other instructions agree with it: docs/operations/slice-test-plan.md step 5 "Wait for the CI build" (:86-89); the card-pass skill's deploy rule (.claude/skills/card-pass/SKILL.md:130-135); and the card runner's standing rule "A green build is not a rolled deploy." (.claude/agents/card-runner.md:152).

Run from the DockerImages checkout against a recent green KubeCoder/Build-Main build (e.g. #551), the script reports kubecoder-dev rolled to that build's pin commit or a descendant. Against a green build whose deploy repo has no clone in this environment's /work, it stops with the missing-clone exit and message: ElectronicsInventory/ElectronicsInventory #255, whose pin line names ElectronicsInventoryDeploy, which is not cloned here. Against DockerImages #2548, which printed ten pin lines, the one stop names every deploy repo not cloned here (all but RegistryDeploy), each with its own `git clone` line.
A real Promote-PRD run prints the handoff line, and track_build.py pointed at that build follows kubecoder-prd to the promoted commit.
items.owed_after: the operator's next KubeCoder/Promote-PRD run (promotion is run by hand; no role in the run promotes)

items.description: Ruling F1: the roll wait is bounded. It has a roll deadline, default 10 minutes and overridable by a flag. After it, the tracker stops with its own exit status, names every app still Progressing, and saves the same evidence as a failed roll.

Ruling F1: a handoff that pushed no new deploy commit has no new sync to wait for. That covers "already carries these pins" (JenkinsPipelineUtils vars/cicd.groovy:114) and a Promote-PRD re-run that only records a release tag (KubeCoderDeploy Jenkinsfile.promote:77-82). The tracker reports each matched app's current sync and health state and returns, rather than waiting on health, even when Argo reports the app Progressing. For "already carries", the state is read against the branch's current head.

Ruling A2: the tracker's PyYAML dependency is declared, not incidental. DockerImages kube-coder-dev-base/Dockerfile installs python3-yaml explicitly. Today it is present only as a dependency of apt yq (kube-coder-dev-base/Dockerfile:47), ubuntu-pro-client and netplan.io.
